summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by the Hamadryad nymphs Atlantia and Phoebe — bride of Istrus son of Egyptus when the ten Arabian-born sons married the Hamadryad maidens at Argos; distinct from Hippodamia daughter of Oenomaus, wife of Pelops, and from Hippodamia bride of Diocorystes.

story.text: Apollodorus pairs Istrus with Hippodamia among the ten sons of Egyptus begotten on an Arabian woman and the ten daughters of Danaus begotten on Hamadryad nymphs. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom.
